title: Impact of Regional Carbon Pricing on CO2 Emissions

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with unit and period fixed effects.

Why:  
• We observe two groups (regions that do and do not adopt carbon pricing) over several time periods, with a single, common adoption date.  
• The interaction term treat_x_post isolates the change in emissions for treated regions after the policy relative to the change in control regions.

Key assumptions:  
1. Parallel trends – in the absence of carbon pricing, treated and control regions would have followed the same emissions trend.  
2. No other contemporaneous, treated-group-specific shocks.  
3. Stable unit treatment value (no spill-overs between regions).

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Difference-in-Differences: Carbon Pricing and Emissions  #
############################################################
# Load (install if necessary) required packages
req_pkgs <- c("fixest", "dplyr")
for(p in req_pkgs){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s37_data.csv")

# 2. Main DID with two-way fixed effects, clustered SE ----------------------
did_main <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data = df,
                  cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n=== Main DID result (clustered by region) ===\n")
print(coeftable(did_main)["treat_x_post", ])

# 3. Robustness checks ------------------------------------------------------

## (a) Cluster by period instead of region
did_timeclu <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                     data = df,
                     cluster = "period")
cat("\n=== Robustness A: cluster by period ===\n")
print(coeftable(did_timeclu)["treat_x_post", ])

## (b) Placebo DID using only pre-treatment periods -------------------------
pre_df <- df %>% 
  filter(post == 0) %>%                     # keep pre-policy observations
  mutate(fake_post  = ifelse(period > median(period), 1, 0),
         fake_int   = treated * fake_post)

placebo <- feols(y ~ fake_int | unit_id + period,
                 data = pre_df,
                 cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n=== Robustness B: placebo interaction in pre-periods ===\n")
print(coeftable(placebo)["fake_int", ])

## (c) Simple DID without fixed effects (naïve spec) ------------------------
did_naive <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
cat("\n=== Robustness C: naïve DID (no FE, HC1 SE) ===\n")
print(coeftest(did_naive, vcov. = vcovHC(did_naive, type = "HC1"))["treat_x_post", ])

# 4. Optional: quick event-study style plot ---------------------------------
# (Requires ggplot2; not essential for numeric output)
if(requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)){
  library(ggplot2)
  df <- df %>% mutate(rel_time = period - min(period))
  es <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
              data = df, cluster = "unit_id")
  ggplot(coefplot(es, keep = "treated::"), 
         aes(x = as.numeric(gsub("treated::rel_time::", "", term)), 
             y = Estimate)) +
    geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), width = .2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Periods relative to policy", y = "Estimate", 
         title = "Event-study coefficients")
}

############################################################
# End of script                                            #
############################################################
```

Running the script prints the main treatment effect followed by three robustness checks (time-clustered SE, placebo, and naïve model). All key results appear in the console.

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. Carbon pricing raises the marginal cost of emitting, so we expect lower CO2 per capita in treated regions post-policy.

Magnitude (log points): Roughly −0.05 to −0.10.  
Interpretation: A coefficient of −0.07 would imply about a 7 % reduction in emissions per capita relative to the counterfactual.  

Placebo interaction should be close to zero and insignificant, supporting the parallel-trends assumption.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in emissions over time between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Regions with carbon pricing show a reduction in CO2 emissions per capita.
